cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same words in front of the Pharisees a second time, and again the point is who gets hurt by the rule. At the table they questioned him for sitting with sinners, and here they condemn men over a fence built around the Sabbath, and he says that knowing the words would have stopped it: *ye would not have condemned the guiltless*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) hands the same words from Hosea to the Pharisees again, saying that knowing them would have kept them from condemning men who broke no commandment.
cards.flag: Describes the Pharisees' Sabbath rule as a fence built around the commandment, not the commandment itself; worth the author's eye.

cards.prose: David says it before the Pharisees did: *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire*. In the same psalm he says what Yahuah (the LORD) wanted in its place, an opened ear and *thy law is within my heart* (Psalm 40:8). That is the mercy over sacrifice Yahusha (Jesus) sends them to learn, the commandment taken in and kept.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: David says sacrifice and offering were not what Yahuah (the LORD) desired, and that he wanted an opened ear and the law kept within the heart.

cards.prose: David carries real guilt in this psalm and says a burnt offering would not answer it: *thou delightest not in burnt offering*. What he brings is named in the next verse, *a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (Psalm 51:17). That is the sick man the physician comes to, not the whole man who thinks he needs none.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: David says he would give the sacrifice if it were wanted, and that what Elohim (God) will not despise is a broken and contrite heart.

cards.prose: The question is Yahuah's (the LORD's) own: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?* The altar was full, and the verse before it sends the people back to *the law of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 1:10), which is where Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Pharisees when he tells them to go and learn.
cards.member_phrase: I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) asks what purpose a multitude of sacrifices serves when he is already full of them and takes no delight in the blood.

cards.prose: Here Yahuah (the LORD) answers an offering that had come loose from obeying him: *Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh*. What he asked at the beginning was *Obey my voice, and I will be your Elohim (God), and ye shall be my people* (Jeremiah 7:23), the thing the Pharisees at the table had put second.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells the people to pile offering on offering and eat the meat, since obeying his voice was what he asked first.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says *I hate, I despise your feast days*, and he is speaking of feasts that were being kept. What he wants instead is *let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (Amos 5:24), the same mercy over sacrifice that Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Pharisees to learn.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he hates and despises feast days kept without justice, and asks for judgment to run down like water.

cards.prose: A worshipper asks whether he comes before Yahuah (the LORD) with burnt offerings and calves of a year old, and the answer comes two verses on: *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). Mercy sits in the middle of that answer, the same word Yahusha (Jesus) gives the Pharisees.
cards.member_phrase: shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?
cards.member_sentence: A worshipper asks whether burnt offerings and year-old calves are how to come before Yahuah (the LORD), and the answer a few verses on is justice, mercy and a humble walk.

cards.prose: The bridegroom Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is no stranger to the room. Yahuah (the LORD) had already said to the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel), *I will betroth thee unto me for ever*, and the gifts he names are *in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies*. The mercy he asks at the table is the mercy of the wedding.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to betroth the scattered house to himself for ever, in righteousness, judgment, lovingkindness and mercies, which is the wedding the bridegroom speaks of.

cards.prose: The husband here is Yahuah (the LORD) himself: *For thy Maker is thine husband*. He speaks to *a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit* (Isaiah 54:6) and says *with great mercies will I gather thee* (Isaiah 54:7). So the bridegroom among the children of the bridechamber is the husband who gathers.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is named as the husband of the forsaken woman, and he will gather her with great mercies.

cards.prose: *Turn, O backsliding children*, he says, *for I am married unto you*. It is a bridegroom speaking to a house that had left him and promising to bring them to Zion a few at a time, *one of a city, and two of a family*. The wedding Yahusha (Jesus) names is that return.
cards.member_phrase: for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells backsliding children he is married to them and will bring them to Zion, taking them one from a city and two from a family.

cards.prose: It is John's disciples who ask why Yahusha's (Jesus's) disciples do not fast, and John had already told them whose wedding it was. He called himself only *the friend of the bridegroom, which standeth and heareth him*, and said he rejoiced greatly at the bridegroom's voice.
cards.member_phrase: the friend of the bridegroom, which standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly
cards.member_sentence: John calls himself the friend of the bridegroom who rejoices at the bridegroom's voice, and so names whose wedding it is.

cards.prose: Paul takes the bridegroom out of the wedding feast and sets him in the household: *Messiah (Christ) also loved the church, and gave himself for it*. That is the other half of what Yahusha (Jesus) said at the table, that the bridegroom would be *taken from them*. The wedding has a cost, and he pays it for the house he came to bring home.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul sets the bridegroom's own love in the household, the husband giving himself for the one he loves.
cards.flag: Kept to the verse's own word 'church' and read the bride as the house of Yashar'el (Israel) being brought home, not a new body; the old note's 'assembly' framing is restated, not extended.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the days of fasting will come when the bridegroom is taken, and here is where they end, with the marriage come and *his wife hath made herself ready*. The mourning that follows the bridegroom's going gives way to gladness.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The marriage of the Lamb has come and his wife is ready, so the time of fasting ends in the feast.

cards.prose: The bride is seen at the end of the story as a city, *prepared as a bride adorned for her husband*, and the voice after it says *Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men* (Revelation 21:3). The bridegroom who was with his friends for a season is with his people to stay.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John sees the holy city coming down from Elohim (God) prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

cards.prose: The two blind men call him *Thou Son of David*, and Isaiah gave that name its root: *a Branch shall grow out of his roots*. What the Branch does is mercy to the poor, for *with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth* (Isaiah 11:4).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah has a rod come out of the stem of Jesse and a Branch grow from his roots, which is where the title Son of David comes from.

cards.prose: *Thou Son of David* is the cry of men who had heard what Jeremiah wrote, that Yahuah (the LORD) would *raise unto David a righteous Branch*. The verse after says *In his days Yahudah (Judah) shall be saved, and Yashar'el (Israel) shall dwell safely* (Jeremiah 23:6), so the one they cry to is king over both houses.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to raise a righteous Branch to David, a king who brings both Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) safe.

cards.prose: Ezekiel names what was done to the sick of the flock, *pushed all the diseased with your horns, till ye have scattered them abroad* (Ezekiel 34:21), and then promises *one shepherd over them*, even David. Two blind men crying for mercy to the Son of David are two of those diseased ones, and he is the shepherd who was promised.
cards.member_phrase: And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) will set up one shepherd, his servant David, over the flock that was pushed about and scattered.

cards.prose: The Son of David in Ezekiel is king over a people made one again, *they shall be no more two nations* (Ezekiel 37:22), and what they do under him is stated plainly, *walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes*. The king the blind men cry to leads people back into the commandments, not out of them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: David my servant is king over the two houses made one, and they walk in Yahuah's (the LORD's) judgments and statutes and do them.

cards.prose: Another cry in nearly the same words, *Have mercy on me, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David*, now from the coast of Tyre and Sidon. She calls him by the title of Yashar'el's (Israel's) king because she is one of the sheep he says he is sent to, *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24).
cards.member_phrase: a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him
cards.member_sentence: A woman from the coast of Tyre and Sidon cries out to Yahusha (Jesus) in the same words, Son of David, have mercy on me.
cards.flag: The old note read her as a marginalized outsider in Hellenistic territory; I wrote her as one of the lost sheep of the scattered house, as the skill reads her.

cards.prose: The same cry again from two blind men, *Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David*, now on the road out of Jericho. The crowd tells them to be quiet and *they cried the more* (Matthew 20:31), and Yahusha (Jesus) stands still and calls them, as he let the first two follow him into the house.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Two blind men cry the same words on the road out of Jericho, and when the crowd hushes them they only cry louder.

cards.prose: What two blind men cried at his heels a whole crowd now cries before him and behind him, *Hosanna to the Son of David*, and they add that he comes *in the name of Yahuah (Lord)*. The title is no longer asked for mercy by a few; it is said over him by the multitudes.
cards.member_phrase: Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord)
cards.member_sentence: The crowds on the road into Jerusalem cry Hosanna to the Son of David and say he comes in the name of Yahuah (the Lord).

cards.prose: The title Yahusha (Jesus) takes at the sick man's bed is Daniel's. Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* before the Ancient of days, and the next verse says what was given him, *dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14). He took on flesh, and that authority is what he uses over the man's sins.
cards.member_phrase: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days and given everlasting dominion, the authority behind the claim at the bed.

cards.prose: At the bed he claimed *power on earth* to forgive sins, and the multitudes *glorified Elohim (God), which had given such power unto men* (Matthew 9:8). On the mountain in Galilee he says the rest of it, *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth*, so the authority shown over one man's sins reaches over everything.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: At the end of Matthew he says all power in heaven and earth is given to him, the whole of what he showed at the bed.

cards.prose: At Zacchaeus's house Yahusha (Jesus) says *he also is a son of Abraham* (Luke 19:9), and names his errand in his own title, as one who *is come to seek and to save*. It is the errand he gave at Matthew's table, *sinners to repentance*, and the lost are sons of Abraham, not strangers.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam says he came to seek and to save the lost, the same errand he gave at Matthew's table.

cards.prose: New wine needs a new container, and Ezekiel says what it is, *a new heart* and *a new spirit*. The wine is not a different law, since the next verse says the spirit will *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The bottle that cannot hold that is the one that breaks.
cards.member_phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit within, the vessel that can hold the commandments kept from the inside.

cards.prose: The new wine is not a new law. Yahusha (Jesus) had already said *I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, and that *one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law* (Matthew 5:18). What cannot hold the wine is a system built on fences, so the container changes and the wine does not.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the new wine is not a new law.

cards.prose: Twelve years of this: the Torah's rule for an issue of blood that runs past its time, *she shall be unclean*. She comes behind him and touches the hem anyway, and her uncleanness does not pass to him; the wholeness passes to her. He did not break the commandment, and he is the one who gave it.
cards.member_phrase: all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean
cards.member_sentence: The Torah's rule on an issue of blood that runs long, which kept the woman unclean for the twelve years she bled.

cards.prose: A leper and a bleeding woman both stand outside by the Torah's own rules, and both come to him. He touches the leper, and the cleanness goes out from him instead of the uncleanness coming in. Then he sends the man to *shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded* (Matthew 8:4), the commandment kept.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: A leper tells Yahusha (Jesus) that if he is willing he can make him clean, another unclean man who comes to him.

cards.prose: The mourners laugh when he says the maid is not dead, *but sleepeth*, yet it is Daniel's own way of speaking of the dead, those who *sleep in the dust of the earth*. For a girl in one house the waking is that he *took her by the hand, and the maid arose* (Matthew 9:25).
cards.member_phrase: many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake
cards.member_sentence: Daniel says many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, the word Yahusha (Jesus) uses of the ruler's daughter.

cards.prose: Isaiah speaks to the dead as sleepers who can be called up, *Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust*, and says *the earth shall cast out the dead*. At the ruler's house he says the maid sleeps and she rises when he takes her by the hand. What the prophet sets at the end of the age shows here in one house, for one girl.
cards.member_phrase: Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah tells those who dwell in dust to awake and sing, and says the earth shall cast out the dead.

cards.prose: He says *sleepeth* of someone who is dead, just as he did of the ruler's daughter, and again the people around him do not take it as he means it, the mourners laughing and the disciples thinking Lazarus is only resting. For him death is a sleep he can wake a man from: *that I may awake him out of sleep*.
cards.member_phrase: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says his friend Lazarus sleepeth and he goes to wake him, using the word he used for the ruler's daughter.

cards.prose: Paul uses the same word for the dead that Yahusha (Jesus) used at the girl's bedside, *asleep*, and writes that the grieving should *sorrow not, even as others which have no hope*. The mourners laughed at the one who said it; Paul hands on what he knew, that the sleep has a waking.
cards.member_phrase: concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope
cards.member_sentence: Paul will not have the brethren ignorant about those who are asleep, so that they do not sorrow as people without hope.

cards.prose: A man both blind and dumb is brought to him and healed so that *the blind and dumb both spake and saw*, and the charge about the prince of the devils follows at once, as it did in Matthew 9. This time he answers it: *Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation* (Matthew 12:25).
cards.member_phrase: he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw
cards.member_sentence: A man both blind and dumb is healed so that he speaks and sees, and the same charge about the prince of the devils follows.

cards.prose: When the charge about the prince of the devils is allowed to stand, this is where it leads. *Whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him* (Matthew 12:32), but naming the work of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) as the devils' work is *the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)*, which shall not be forgiven.
cards.member_phrase: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men
cards.member_sentence: He says every sin and blasphemy can be forgiven except blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), after his works were called the prince of devils' doing.

cards.prose: When Matthew gives the charge in full it has a name, *but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils* (Matthew 12:24), and the name is older than the Pharisees. A king of Samaria sent to ask *Baal-zebub the god of Ekron* whether he would recover, when he should have asked Yahuah (the LORD). The charge borrows that name and puts it on the one who casts devils out.
cards.member_phrase: enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease
cards.member_sentence: A king of Samaria sends to Baal-zebub the god of Ekron to ask whether he will recover, the name behind the charge of the prince of the devils.

cards.prose: Matthew's *scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd* is Zechariah's picture of a people who *went their way as a flock*. Idols and diviners comforted *in vain*, and the next verse turns on the shepherds, *Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds* (Zechariah 10:3).
cards.member_phrase: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah says the people went their way as a flock, troubled because there was no shepherd, after idols and diviners comforted in vain.

cards.prose: The harvest he calls plenteous in Matthew, he tells his disciples to see for themselves, to *Lift up your eyes* because the fields are *white already to harvest*. The ripeness is there before they have done anything, and he says they enter in where *other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours* (John 4:38).
cards.member_phrase: Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest
cards.member_sentence: He tells his disciples the fields are already white to harvest, the same harvest he calls plenteous.

cards.prose: The twelve are the answer to the prayer. He had just said *the labourers are few*, and now he calls twelve and gives them power *against unclean spirits*, and over every sickness, the work he had been doing himself in every city and village. They are given his own work to do.
cards.member_phrase: he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease
cards.member_sentence: He calls the twelve and gives them power over unclean spirits and every sickness, the answer to his request for labourers.
